title: Attention stride optimizer and MIG burst resilience
creator: Ava Chen
description: Optimize runtime kernel selection for variable-stride attention patterns and harden prefill/decode scheduling to tolerate short-duration bandwidth/clock perturbations on mixed MIG partitions across H100, L40S and A10 fleets.
background: We observe tail-latency spikes and throughput regression for certain conversational workloads when requests are routed to GPU nodes with heavily fragmented MIG partitions or when clocks fluctuate due to thermal headroom changes. Existing kernel selection favors a single high-throughput microkernel that performs poorly for sparse/strided attention and suffers under intermittent NVLink contention. This ticket groups experiments, a lightweight selector, and scheduling mitigations to reduce p99 latency and improve throughput stability across mixed SKU fleets.
goals: Introduce a fast attention-stride classifier to pick between dense-prefill and stride-optimized kernels at runtime
Add a short-horizon MIG burst resilience policy in the prefill scheduler to avoid entering fragile kernel modes during clock oscillation
Validate across H100/L40S/A10 mixed-fleet traces and show p99 improvement of >=15% for tail-sensitive chat workloads
Keep p50 latency within 5% of baseline while improving p99 and throughput stability
non_goals: Full rewrite of attention kernels (this is optimizer/selector + scheduling adjustments)
Changing model weights or quantization schemes (fallback tuning only)
design_notes: Design a two-stage selector: a very cheap stride fingerprinter (first N tokens KV density + token stride histogram) that runs in prefill then annotates request metadata, followed by a kernel lookup table keyed by (model-arch, seq_len_bucket, stride_class, MIG_topology_hint). Provide a soft-fallback path: when clocks or NVLink telemetry indicate instability, prefer conservative kernel + smaller micro-batches and enable a brief preemptive KV-cache prefetch window. The prefetch window length is adjustable via autoscaling policy parameters.
decisions: Use a lightweight fingerprint (byte-level token spacing + attention mask sampling) implemented in C++ in the serving hot path
Expose a runtime knob to favor stability-over-throughput during detected MIG/clock oscillations
Telemetry signals used: per-GPU clock changes > 5% within 500ms, NVLink retransmit rate spike, MIG partition occupancy > 85%
tradeoffs: Aggressively switching to stable kernels reduces maximum achievable throughput for steady-state fully-dense workloads. We will gate the behavior behind an adaptive hysteresis window and profile-guided thresholds per SKU to keep regressions within the 5% p50 budget.
implementation_plan: 1) Implement stride fingerprint and kernel LUT (week 1). 2) Integrate telemetry hooks and MIG topology hint propagation (week 2). 3) Implement scheduler soft-fallback and prefetch window logic (week 3). 4) Run mixed-sku soak tests and A/B on a subset of production fleet (week 4).
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency decreased by >=15% on representative conversational traces compared to current baseline for H100 and L40S nodes
p50 latency regression <=5% on dense workloads
No increase in OOM incidents during test runs
Scheduler fallback triggers are auditable in Console traces and correlate with the telemetry signals defined
PRs merged with unit + integration tests and benchmarks recorded in perf dashboard
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created after triage with perf and infra teams
2025-02-18: Prototype stride fingerprint implemented; microbenchmark shows selector overhead ~45ns per request on warm path
2025-02-22: Added MIG topology hint propagation to request metadata; identified a race when partition state changes rapidly — mitigated by adding version tag to hint
2025-02-26: Early A/B run on a 10% canary of H100 fleet; observed p99 down 12% but p50 increased 3% on one workload; adjusted hysteresis and micro-batch sizing
2025-03-04: Extended tests to mixed H100/L40S nodes; NVLink spike simulations reproduced tail events and scheduler fallback prevented most spikes
benchmark_summary: Canary A/B on H100: dense-chat workload p99 reduced 18% with selector + fallback; throughput stable for mixed-batch workloads. On L40S, p99 reduced 11% with conservative thresholds. A10 showed modest gains for medium sequence lengths but requires tuned micro-batching to avoid p50 regressions.
risks: Selector misclassification for short contexts may cause unnecessary kernel switches (mitigated by min-token threshold)
Telemetry noise leading to oscillatory fallback on nodes with marginally fluctuating clocks (mitigated with hysteresis and min-duration windows)
Edge-case models with custom attention masks could produce poor stride fingerprints — plan to whitelist known models
QA_plan: Create regression suite with 6 representative prompts (short/long/dense/sparse) and run on H100/L40S/A10 combos under simulated clock/NVLink noise. Add unit tests for fingerprint determinism and integration tests for scheduler hysteresis behavior.
next_steps: Finish integration tests and telemetry dashboard panels
Rollout to 25% canary with runtime-1.22 on dedicated fleet
Prepare runbook for operations if fallback triggers excessively (include knob to force-stable or force-performance)
